sections.h2: Who records a deed for a house in St. Louis County?
sections.html:
The St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds records it, but only for land outside the City of St. Louis. The office is at 41 South Central Avenue in Clayton, the county seat, and its county page lists the phone as (314) 615-7100 and the hours as Monday through Thursday, 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m.

The same office files subdivision plats, federal and state tax liens and other written instruments that affect real property or personal property, and it issues marriage licenses. Every recorded document is open for public research. If you sell a house in one of the county's municipalities, such as Florissant, Chesterfield or Ballwin, the deed goes here, and the buyer's title company normally handles the filing for you.

sections.h2: How much does the county charge to record a deed?
sections.html:
The county's cost page lists $26 for the first page and $3 for each additional page. A $25 non-standard fee is added when the document does not meet the Missouri formatting standards. Recording through an e-recording vendor can add the vendor's own charges.

State law sits behind the formatting rule. RSMo 59.310 lets a recorder refuse a document that fails its standards, or record it for an extra $25. Quick reference for what a deed packet in this county tends to involve:

  • Pages printed on one side only, on white or light paper, with no permanent binding.
  • Type no smaller than eight-point, in black or dark ink.
  • A blank top margin of at least three inches for the recorder's stamp, and three-quarters of an inch on the other sides.
  • On the first page below the top margin: the document title, its date, the grantors and their marital status, the grantees, any statutory addresses and the legal description.

If you overpay, the county's refund page says overages under $10 are not refunded, while larger overages come back by check.

sections.h2: What is the difference between the county recorder and the city recorder?
sections.html:
St. Louis city and St. Louis County are separate governments with separate land records offices. Residents of the city voted in 1877 to leave the county and become an independent city, so a house on one side of the line is recorded in a different office than a house on the other side.

The City of St. Louis Recorder of Deeds takes documents at City Hall, Room 126, 1200 Market Street, and its land records page prices a standard deed differently from the county. Check the parcel's address before you send anything anywhere.

sections.h2: How do I submit a deed to the St. Louis County recorder?
sections.html:
You can mail or drop off the original notarized document at the Clayton office, with a check or money order made payable to ROD for the recording cost. The county's how-to page says the original comes back to you within a week of the recording date. The other route is online through a third-party e-recording vendor from the county's list.

The county directs businesses that prefer electronic submission to contact one of its vendors to set that up, so a seller handling one deed will usually go by mail or leave it to the closing agent. The easiest path is to let the closing agent record the deed and send you a copy.

Does the county charge a separate transfer tax at recording? The cost page shows recording charges only. Ask the Recorder's office at (314) 615-7100, or the title company handling your sale, whether any other charge applies to your particular deed.

sections.h2: How do I get a copy of my deed or search old records?
sections.html:
Order a certified copy online through the county's vendor, or request one in person. In-person copy payments are by credit or debit card only. The county's deed copy page prices copies at $2 for the first page and $1 for each additional page, with a typical printed deed at $5 plus a convenience fee and an extra $1 for each certified copy.

  • Recorded deeds can be searched online back to 1974.
  • For a property bought before 1974, make an appointment for a deed search at the Clayton office.
  • You can also schedule an appointment if you would rather search in person than use the web app.

A recent deed copy is worth having when you sell, because the buyer's title company will compare the legal description and the owner names against it.

sections.h2: What happens if the recorder rejects my deed?
sections.html:
Under RSMo 59.310 the recorder sends a rejected document back to the person who presented it, with a written reason. A fixed document can then be presented again. The statute also allows a non-conforming document to be recorded for the extra $25 instead of being turned away.

The statute also lists documents that are exempt from the format rules and that a recorder may still record. Examples include documents signed before January 1, 2002, documents executed outside the United States, certified copies, and a document where one of the original parties is deceased or otherwise incapacitated. An heir selling a parent's house may run into the last category, so mention it to the title company early.

Keep the recorded copy with your sale file. The three-inch top margin is reserved for the recorder's certification, so the stamped copy is your proof that the deed was filed.

sections.h2: What does the county look like for someone selling a house here?
sections.html:
St. Louis County sits in eastern Missouri between the Missouri River on the north, the Meramec River on the south and the Mississippi River and City of St. Louis on the east. The Census Bureau's QuickFacts table estimates 990,911 residents for July 2025, spread over 507.88 square miles of land, and counts 448,637 housing units.

About 69.2% of households own the home they live in, and the median owner-occupied home is valued at $276,800 for 2020 to 2024. Median household income is $82,936. Median gross rent is $1,209.

The county contains 87 municipal governments, and about a third of residents live in unincorporated areas where the county handles zoning and code enforcement. Twenty-three public school districts serve it, including Clayton, Kirkwood, Parkway, Rockwood and Webster Groves, so the buyer of your house will often ask about the district first.

Because the recorder is a county office, a deed for a house in Clayton and one for a house in Wildwood are filed at the same counter, even though the two municipalities govern the property separately. Ask the municipality's city hall about local steps before you list.

faqs.q: Where is the St. Louis County Recorder of Deeds office?
faqs.a: It is at 41 South Central Avenue, Clayton, MO 63105. The county lists Monday through Thursday hours of 8 a.m. to 3:30 p.m., the phone (314) 615-7100 and the email Recorder@stlouiscountymo.gov.

faqs.q: What does recording a deed cost in St. Louis County?
faqs.a: The county lists $26 for the first page and $3 for each additional page, plus a $25 non-standard fee if the document misses the Missouri formatting standards. E-recording vendors may add their own fees.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed by mail?
faqs.a: Yes. Send the original notarized deed with a check or money order payable to ROD to the Clayton office. The county says the original is returned within one week of the recording date.

faqs.q: Is a house inside the City of St. Louis recorded here?
faqs.a: No. The City of St. Louis has its own Recorder of Deeds at City Hall, Room 126, with a different fee schedule. Only parcels outside the city limits but inside the county go to the Clayton office.

faqs.q: How far back can I search deeds online?
faqs.a: The county says recorded deeds are available online through 1974. For a purchase before 1974, make an appointment for a deed search at the Clayton office.
